### 1. The Portrait of a Lady (Prose)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**The Grandmother**

**Village Life**

**City Life**

**Death**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Khushwant Singh is a famous Indian writer.
He writes about his sweet old grandmother.

**The Grandmother**
The grandmother was short, fat, and bent.
She wore a white saree and counted prayer beads.
Her white hair made her look calm and peaceful.

**Village Life**
In the village, they were best friends.
She got him ready and walked him to school.
She read holy books and fed chapatis to street dogs.

**City Life**
They moved to the city and their life changed.
He went to an English school by bus.
She could not help him and fed sparrows instead.

**Death**
He came back from college and she fell sick.
She lay in bed, prayed, and died peacefully.
Her prayer beads fell from her hand.

**Conclusion**
Thousands of sparrows came and sat near her body.
They did not eat bread and sat in silence.
They flew away quietly when her body was taken.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Portrait | உருவப்படம் |
| Wrinkles | முகச்சுருக்கங்கள் |
| Scriptures | புனித நூல்கள் |
| Mourn | துக்கம் அனுசரிப்பது |
| Sparrows | சிட்டுக்குருவிகள் |

### 2. The Queen of Boxing (Prose)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Early Life**

**Getting Money**

**The Big Match**

**The Queen Title**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
M. C. Mary Kom is a famous Indian boxer.
She is from a state called Manipur.

**Early Life**
Mary Kom came from a very poor family.
Her parents worked hard in fields.
She did boxing in secret because her father disliked it.

**Getting Money**
She was selected to play a match in the USA.
She did not have money for the plane ticket.
Her father and village friends collected cash for her.

**The Big Match**
In America, she lost her bags and did not like the food.
She did not give up and played well.
She won a silver medal in her first try.

**The Queen Title**
She worked hard and won many gold medals.
People called her "Magnificent Mary."
She became the "Queen of Boxing."

**Conclusion**
Her life shows that hard work can beat poverty.
She proved that Indian women can win big in sports.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Autobiography | சுயசரிதை |
| Struggle | போராட்டம் |
| Determination | மன உறுதி |
| Magnificent | மிகச்சிறந்த |
| Poverty | வறுமை |

### 3. Forgetting (Prose)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Good Memory**

**Common Mistakes**

**Letters and Medicine**

**Why We Forget**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Robert Lynd is a famous Irish writer.
He writes funny stories about everyday habits.

**Good Memory**
Human memory is actually very good.
People remember phone numbers and actor names.
They remember their daily work easily.

**Common Mistakes**
But people forget small things.
They leave umbrellas and bags on trains.
Sportsmen leave bats and balls behind.

**Letters and Medicine**
People forget to take their medicine on time.
The author forgets to post letters.
He keeps letters in his pocket for days.

**Why We Forget**
We forget when our mind has other deep thoughts.
A wise man forgets items because he thinks of big things.
A lover forgets because he thinks of his lover.

**Conclusion**
Forgetting is not always a bad thing.
It does not mean a person is silly.
It shows that the mind is busy with creative thoughts.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Forgetting | மறதி |
| Memory | ஞாபகசக்தி |
| Routine | தினசரி வேலைகள் |
| Confess | ஒப்புக்கொள்வது |
| Absent-minded | கவனக்குறைவு |

### 4. A Tight Corner (Prose)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Meaning of Tight Corner**

**The Art Shop**

**The Big Mistake**

**The Safe Escape**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
E. V. Lucas is a famous English writer.
He writes interesting stories about real life.

**Meaning of Tight Corner**
A "tight corner" means a very difficult situation.
The author says money trouble is the worst tight corner.

**The Art Shop**
The author went to a big art auction shop.
He had only 63 pounds in his bank.
He did not want to buy anything.

**The Big Mistake**
Just for fun, he bid on an expensive painting.
He thought rich people would bid more.
Suddenly, the bidding stopped and he won it for 4,000 pounds.

**The Safe Escape**
He was scared because he had no money to pay.
A rich man who missed the shop came to him.
The man bought the painting from him and gave him extra money.

**Conclusion**
Luck saved the author from a big insult.
He promised never to play foolish games again.

|---|---|

### 5. The Convocation Address (Prose)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Meaning of University**

**Advice to Students**

**Duties to Society**

**Role of Leaders**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Dr. Arcot Ramasamy Mudaliar was a great Indian lawyer and speaker.
This speech is his advice to young students graduating from college.

**Meaning of University**
A university is not just a place to get degree certificates.
It is a place that prepares students for a better life.
It teaches how to think clearly and choose the right path.

**Advice to Students**
Students must be honest and disciplined in life.
They should read books even after finishing college.
They must always speak the truth and do good work.

**Duties to Society**
The country spends money on your higher education.
So, students must serve the poor and helpless people.
Students should help to make India a strong and peaceful nation.

**Role of Leaders**
The country needs good and unselfish leaders.
True leaders work for the happiness of all people.
Education must make students into good citizens and leaders.

**Conclusion**
The speech teaches us that education is a lifelong duty.
Students must use their knowledge to shine bright and serve the world.

#### 📖 Key Words

|---|---|
| Convocation | பட்டமளிப்பு விழா |
| Address | உரையாற்றுதல் / சொற்பொழிவு |
| Discipline | ஒழுக்கம் |

| Service | சேவை |

### 6. The Accidental Tourist (Prose)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Travel Confusion**

**The Bag Incident**

**The Plane Accidents**

**Missing Out**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Bill Bryson is a famous American writer.
He writes funny stories about his real travel experiences.

**Travel Confusion**
The author gets easily confused when he travels.
He forgets his hotel room numbers and gets lost near toilets.
He cannot do simple things that other people do easily.

**The Bag Incident**
Once at an airport, his carry-on bag got stuck.
He pulled it hard, and the zipper broke open completely.
All his things, like coins, newspapers, and tobacco, flew everywhere.
His finger started bleeding, and he panicked in front of everyone. [1]

**The Plane Accidents**
He always makes messes inside airplanes.
Once, he knocked over a soft drink onto a lady twice.
Another time, his seat sucked his coat and trapped him.
He even got his mouth covered in black ink while sucking his pen.

**Missing Out**
Because of his clumsy mistakes, his family stays careful.
His wife asks the kids to cut the food for their father.
He also loses his flyer points because his name is written wrong on tickets.

**Conclusion**
The story tells us that travel is not fun for everyone.
The author uses humor to show his weakness in managing daily travel life.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Accidental | தற்செயலாக / எதிர்பாராமல் நடக்கும் |
| Tourist | சுற்றுலாப் பயணி |
| Confusion | குழப்பம் |
| Bleeding | ரத்தம் வடிதல் |
| Clumsy | தடுமாற்றமான / கவனக்குறைவான |

## 📝 Poem Paragraphs


### 1. Once Upon a Time (Poem)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Past Laughter**

**Fake Manners**

**Many Faces**

**Wanting to Change**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Gabriel Okara is a famous poet from Nigeria.
He writes about how modern life changes people.

**Past Laughter**
In the old days, people laughed with real joy.
Today, adults smile only with their teeth.
Their eyes stay cold and unfriendly.

**Fake Manners**
People are not true friends anymore.
They shake hands but look at your money.
They say "come again" but lock their doors.

**Many Faces**
The father also learned to be fake.
He changes his face like changing clothes.
He has different smiles for work and parties.

**Wanting to Change**
He looks at his small son's innocent face.
He feels bad about his own fake smiles.
He wants to forget his bad adult habits.

**Conclusion**
The father asks his son to teach him.
He wants to learn how to laugh naturally again.
He wants his pure childhood heart back.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Innocence | கபமற்ற / தூய்மையான குened |
| Hypocrisy | போலித்தனம் |
| Fake | உண்மையானது அல்லாத |
| Unlearn | கெட்ட பழக்கங்களை மறப்பது |

### 2. Confessions of a Born Spectator (Poem)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**The Poet's Choice**

**Hard Games**

**Getting Hurt**

**Sitting Safely**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Ogden Nash is a famous American poet.
He writes funny poems about people.

**The Poet's Choice**
The poet loves to watch sports.
He does not want to play games.
He is happy to be a fan in the stands.

**Hard Games**
Athletes run fast and play hard.
They play football, hockey, and basketball.
The poet likes them but will not swap places.

**Getting Hurt**
Players play very rough.
They hurt their knees, hands, and faces.
They do not care about hurting others.

**Sitting Safely**
The poet's body wants to stay safe.
He likes to sit, eat, and drink with friends.
He pays for tickets but stays off the field.

**Conclusion**
Some people play and some people watch.
The poet accepts his role happily.
He chooses comfort over sports fame.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Confession | ஒப்புதல் |
| Spectator | வேடிக்கை பார்ப்பவர் |

| Admire | வியந்து பார்ப்பது |

### 3. Lines Written in Early Spring (Poem)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Nature's Beauty**

**Nature's Joy**

**Man's Sadness**

**Nature's Plan**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
William Wordsworth is a great English poet.
People call him the "Poet of Nature."

**Nature's Beauty**
The poet sits under some trees in spring.
He looks around at the beautiful world.
He sees lovely flowers and green trees breathing fresh air.

**Nature's Joy**
Every living thing in nature is happy.
Small birds hop and play around him.
Tree branches open up to catch the wind.

**Man's Sadness**
This beautiful scene makes the poet sad.
He thinks about human society.
He feels bad about how humans fight and hurt each other.

**Nature's Plan**
The poet believes God made nature to be happy.
Nature wants all creatures to live in peace.
Humans are sad because they do not follow nature.

**Conclusion**
Nature is a place of true joy and peace.
Humans must stop wars and live in love.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Grove | சிறு தோப்பு |
| Spring | வசந்த காலம் |
| Twigs | சிறிய கிளைகள் |
| Grief | துக்கம் / மனவருத்தம் |

### 4. Macavity – The Mystery Cat (Poem)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**The Hidden Paw**

**Breaking Laws**

**Appearance**

**Master of Tricks**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
T. S. Eliot is a very famous English poet.
He wrote this funny poem about a cat.

**The Hidden Paw**
Macavity is a mystery cat called the "Hidden Paw."
He is a master criminal who does bad things.
He never leaves any footprints or clues behind.

**Breaking Laws**
Macavity breaks human laws and the law of gravity.
He can float in the air without falling down.
The London police can never catch him.

**Appearance**
Macavity is a very tall, thin ginger cat.
His eyes are sunken in, and his brow is deep in thought.
His coat is dirty and his whiskers are messy.

**Master of Tricks**
He moves his head side to side like a snake.
When he looks half-asleep, he is wide awake.
He looks like a normal cat but he is an evil monster inside.

**Conclusion**
Macavity always escapes from the crime scene.
The poem uses fun lines to show an uncatchable criminal cat.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Mystery | மர்மம் |
| Gravity | புவிஈர்ப்பு விசை |
| Fakir | சாமியார் / துறவி |

### 5. Everest Is Not The Only Peak (Poem)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Meaning of Success**

**Small but Honest Work**

**True Human Worth**

**Staying Proud**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
Kulothungan is the pen name of Professor V. C. Kulandaiswamy.
He is a famous Tamil scholar and poet who wrote in English too.

**Meaning of Success**
Mount Everest is the highest mountain, but it is not the only peak.
Every small hill has its own beauty and height.
Similarly, you do not need to be the topmost person to be successful.

**Small but Honest Work**
Doing small work with honesty is better than doing big, wrong work.
We must respect people who work hard every day.
Reaching a lower peak with self-respect is a grand victory.

**True Human Worth**
A person's value is not measured by money or position.
It is measured by their good character and dedication.
We must adore people who do their duties perfectly.

**Staying Proud**
We should never feel low if we fail to reach the top.
We must stand tall and feel proud of our honest efforts.
Virtue and honor are the true peaks of human life.

**Conclusion**
The poem tells us to appreciate every honest human effort.
Every good human being is a winner in life.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Peak | சிகரம் |
| Adore | போற்றுதல் / மதித்தல் |
| Virtue | நற்பண்பு / ஒழுக்கம் |
| Honest | நேர்மையான |

### 6. The Hollow Crown (Poem)


**Plan of the Paragraph**

**Introduction**

**Sadness of Kings**

**Death the Conqueror**

**The Hollow Crown**

**Real Human Truth**

**Conclusion**

**Introduction**
William Shakespeare is the world-famous English playwright and poet.
This poem is a small part from his famous history play Richard II.

**Sadness of Kings**
King Richard is very sad because he lost his power.
He tells his friends to sit on the ground and talk about dead kings.
Some kings were killed in war, and some were poisoned by wives.

**Death the Conqueror**
Death is the supreme king over all human rulers.
Death sits inside the hollow crown of a mortal king.
Death laughs at the king's false power and high pride.

**The Hollow Crown**
A crown looks big but it is hollow (empty) inside.
It gives a king a small time to act like a god on earth.
At the end, Death comes with a small pin, breaks the castle wall, and kills the king.

**Real Human Truth**
The king tells his friends not to bow or respect him anymore.
He says he is just a normal human being who needs bread and feels pain.
He has tastes, wants, and needs friends just like ordinary people.

**Conclusion**
The poem shows that death treats kings and beggars the same way.
Power and crowns are temporary, but death is permanent.

#### 📖 Key Words
| English | Tamil |
|---|---|
| Hollow | வெற்று / காலியான |
| Crown | கிரீடம் |
| Mortal | அழியக்கூடிய |
| Pride | பெருமை / கர்வம் |

the school canteen.
Arun Kumar
School Sports Captain

Describe a process

**Q:** Describe the process of preparing a cup of tea.

**A:** 
First, pour one cup of water into a small pan and light the stove.
Next, add one teaspoon of tea leaves to the water and let it boil.
Then, add half a cup of milk and one teaspoon of sugar to the boiling water.
After that, let the whole mixture boil together for two minutes.
Finally, turn off the stove, strain the tea into a cup using a filter, and serve hot

### Dialogue writing


### Example 1: Between a Teacher and a Student


**Q:** Write a conversation between a student and a teacher. The student needs more time to finish their homework.

**A:** 
Rohan: Good morning, Sir.
Teacher: Good morning, Rohan. Where is your English project?
Rohan: I am sorry, Sir. I did not finish it today.
Teacher: Why did you not finish it? Today is the last date.
Rohan: Sir, I had a bad fever for two days. I could not write.
Teacher: Oh, I see. You can submit it this Thursday.
Rohan: Thank you so much, Sir! I will bring it on Thursday.

### Example 2: Between Two Friends


**Q:** Write a conversation between two friends talking about their school exams.

**A:** 
Anand: Hi Ramesh! Are you ready for the exams next week?
Ramesh: Hi Anand! No, I am very scared. English grammar is very hard for me.
Anand: Do not worry. Which topic is difficult?
Ramesh: I do not understand Active and Passive voice. What about you?
Anand: I know grammar, but I cannot memorize the long prose answers.
Ramesh: Let us study together at your house this evening. We can help each other.
Anand: That is a great idea! See you at 5:00 PM today.
Ramesh: Perfect. See you then. Bye!

### Expansion of Proverbs

### 1. A Bad Workman Always Blames His Tools

The meaning of this proverb is that our success does not depend on what kind of tools we have but how we use them. Here is a story to elucidate the meaning.

Raj and Ravi were farmers. They owned a pair of oxen each with which they ploughed their lands. Raj put in hard work while Ravi hardly worked. Raj worked all day long, aimed at getting a good yield and took good care of his oxen, fully understanding their needs. Ravi, on the other hand, was very lazy and miserly. He never fed his oxen well but exploited them to the maximum.

As a true friend, Raj advised Ravi and sometimes even admonished him for his treatment of the animals. Ravi paid little heed to Raj’s words. He soon bought a tractor to plough his land and chased the oxen away. Raj brought home the animals and took care of them too though he could not afford it. The monsoon soon arrived and it was time for cultivation. Raj’s land was well-ploughed and ready for cultivation-thanks to his oxen.

Ravi in his miserly fashion had not maintained his tractor well and it kept giving him trouble. As a result, he could not get his field ready for cultivation on time. He lamented and blamed it all on bad luck not realizing that it was he who was responsible for his miserable state. Ravi not only lost out on a good yield because of his laziness, but also spent a huge sum of money to repair his tractor due to poor maintenance. Despite having better equipment Ravi was unable to get the best results. But, Raj was a good workman and hence was able to succeed with the limited resources he had.

**IT IS NEVER TOO LATE TO MEND**

### 2. Actions Speak Louder Than Words

The proverb ‘Actions speak louder than words’ means “If we want to help somebody, it must be through action giving money or things not simply by empty words. A friend in need is a friend indeed”. Let us see the meaning of this proverb in the following story.

A small town was hit by famine, because of lack of adequate rain. People were suffering. There was no enough rice for hundreds of people. The Church Father knelt down and prayed to god for them: 'God almighty, help these poor people. Save them from famine' and so many other touching words. In his granary there were hundred sacks of rice.

A rich man who had a few sacks of rice invited all the towns’ people to his house and distributed rice to them free of cost. Then he went to the church Father and said to him, 'Good morning Father. Please excuse me father. You are praying for the poor people - it is good. But if you take rice from your granary and give it to the poor people, it will be better.' The Father realised the truth and opened his granary to the poor. So, actions speak better than words.

**BARE WORDS BUY NO BARLEY**

### 3. Despair Gives Courage to a Coward

Despair gives courage to a coward means “Even a coward will act bravely in a hopeless, dangerous situation.” The following story reveals this proverb.

Ganesh was a ten-year old boy. He was a coward, he was afraid of many things. All his friends climbed up the trees, jumped from branch to branch, plucked fruits and flowers. Thus they enjoyed themselves. But Ganesh went near a tree. He always said, “If I climb up a tree, I may fall down and die”. His friends encouraged him, but in vain.

One day Edwin was walking across the field. A bull saw him and began to chase him. He ran faster and faster, but the bull also ran faster after him. Suddenly he saw a tree. He jumped on to the tree, put his arms around the trunk of the tree, moving up with great difficulty and strain, he reached the first branch and sat on it. The bull went away.

In a minute, all his friends came there “Hi, Ganesh!” “What a surprise!” Ganesh jumped down and narrated the whole event. Then his friends exclaimed: “Despair gives courage even to a coward.”

**COURAGE CONQUERS ALL THINGS**

### Reading comprehension Exam Passage: The Life of Honeybees

Honeybees are highly social insects that live in well-organized colonies called beehives. A single hive can contain up to 60,000 bees, divided into three distinct types: the Queen, the Workers, and the Drones. The Queen is the largest bee and is responsible for laying thousands of eggs daily. The female Worker bees do all the actual work, such as collecting pollen from flowers, building the honeycomb, and protecting the hive from enemies. The male Drones exist solely to mate with the queen. Bees communicate with each other using a special series of movements known as the "waggle dance," which tells other hive members the exact location of food sources.

### Questions and Answers

**Q:** What are the three types of bees found in a beehive?
**A:** The three types of bees found in a beehive are the Queen, the Workers, and the Drones.

**Q:** What is the main responsibility of the Queen bee?
**A:** The main responsibility of the Queen bee is to lay thousands of eggs daily.

**Q:** Mention any two duties performed by the female Worker bees.
**A:** Two duties performed by the Worker bees are collecting pollen from flowers and protecting the hive from enemies.

**Q:** How do honeybees communicate the location of food sources to one another?
**A:** Honeybees communicate the location of food sources using a special series of movements known as the "waggle dance."

**Q:** Find a word in the passage which means "groups of insects living together."
**A:** Colonies (or colonies).
